metadata.name: NIST Cryptographic Algorithm Rules
sources: NIST SP 800-131A Rev.2 (March 2019) - Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths
NIST SP 800-131A Rev.3 IPD (October 2024) - Initial Public Draft
NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 - Recommendation for Key Management
NIST SP 800-90A Rev.1 - Recommendation for Random Number Generation Using DRBGs
NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2 - Guidelines for TLS Implementations
NIST SP 800-132 - Recommendation for Password-Based Key Derivation
metadata.description: Machine-readable ruleset derived from official NIST publications for detecting cryptographic vulnerabilities in Python source code. Every rule cites the exact NIST section it is derived from.

rules.description: Two-key and three-key TDEA (DES/3DES) encryption is disallowed for applying cryptographic protection. TDEA was deprecated and is now fully disallowed after December 31, 2023 per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 2.
rules.remediation: Use AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 as specified in FIPS 197. Example: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.algorithms import AES

rules.description: SKIPJACK encryption is disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 2. It is a classified NSA cipher formally disallowed by NIST for all applications.
rules.remediation: Use AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 as specified in FIPS 197.

rules.description: AES ECB (Electronic Codebook) mode is disallowed for encryption per SP 800-131A Rev.3 IPD Section 2.2. ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks, revealing data patterns and providing no semantic security.
rules.remediation: Use AES-GCM (authenticated encryption) or AES-CBC with a random IV. Example: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers import modes; modes.GCM(nonce)

rules.description: Blowfish is not included in any NIST-approved algorithm list. It uses a 64-bit block size making it vulnerable to birthday attacks (SWEET32 attack). Only AES is NIST-approved for symmetric encryption per FIPS 197.
rules.remediation: Use AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 (FIPS 197).

rules.description: RC2 and RC4 (ARC4) are not NIST-approved algorithms. RC4 has multiple critical cryptographic weaknesses and is prohibited in all modern security standards. Neither appears in any NIST-approved algorithm list.
rules.remediation: Use AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 (FIPS 197).

rules.description: MD5 is not approved for any security application per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 9. It is vulnerable to collision and preimage attacks and does not appear in FIPS 180-4 approved hash functions.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 as specified in FIPS 180-4. Example: hashlib.sha256(data)

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 9; SP 800-131A Rev.3 IPD Section 9
rules.description: SHA-1 is disallowed for digital signature generation per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 9. Per Rev.3 IPD, SHA-1 is deprecated for all non-digital-signature cryptographic protection through December 31, 2030 and disallowed thereafter.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4) or SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512 (FIPS 202). Example: hashlib.sha256(data)

rules.description: SHA-224 (224-bit output) is deprecated through December 31, 2030 and disallowed thereafter per SP 800-131A Rev.3 IPD Section 9. The 224-bit security margin is considered insufficient for long-term security.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4). Example: hashlib.sha256(data)

rules.description: RIPEMD-160 and Whirlpool are not NIST-approved hash functions. FIPS 180-4 only approves SHA-2 family and FIPS 202 approves SHA-3 family.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4). Example: hashlib.sha256(data)

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 5, Table 4; SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 5.6
rules.description: RSA key sizes less than 2048 bits are disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 5. Keys of 512 and 1024 bits provide fewer than 80 bits of security strength and are vulnerable to factorization attacks. SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 5.6 requires minimum 2048-bit keys.
rules.remediation: Use RSA with minimum 2048-bit key size. 3072 or 4096 bits recommended for long-term security. Example: rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)

rules.description: PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA padding is disallowed after December 31, 2023 per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 6. It is vulnerable to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext padding oracle attacks.
rules.remediation: Use RSA-OAEP for encryption or RSA-PSS for signatures. Example: padding.OAEP(mgf=padding.MGF1(algorithm=hashes.SHA256()), algorithm=hashes.SHA256(), label=None)

rules.description: DSA for signature generation is retired per SP 800-131A Rev.3 IPD Section 3 and FIPS 186-5. DSA has been removed from the approved signature generation algorithm list.
rules.remediation: Use ECDSA with NIST P-256, P-384, or P-521 curves, or RSA-PSS. Example: ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 3; SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 5.6
rules.description: Elliptic curves with field sizes below 224 bits provide less than 112 bits of security strength and are disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 3. These curves do not meet the minimum security strength requirement in SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 5.6.
rules.remediation: Use NIST-approved curves: P-256 (SECP256R1), P-384 (SECP384R1), or P-521 (SECP521R1). Example: ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())

rules.description: Diffie-Hellman modulus length below 2048 bits is disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 4 and SP 800-56A Rev.3. Small DH parameters are vulnerable to the Logjam attack and discrete logarithm computation.
rules.remediation: Use DH parameters with at least 2048-bit modulus. Example: dh.generate_parameters(generator=2, key_size=2048)

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-90A Rev.1 Section 1; SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 8
rules.description: Python's random module uses the Mersenne Twister PRNG which is NOT a NIST-approved Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG). SP 800-90A Rev.1 specifies approved DRBGs: CTR_DRBG (AES), Hash_DRBG, and HMAC_DRBG. Using non-approved PRNGs for security purposes violates SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 8.
rules.remediation: Use the secrets module or os.urandom() for cryptographic operations. Example: import secrets; secrets.token_bytes(32) or secrets.randbelow(n)

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 8; SP 800-90A Rev.1 Section 3
rules.description: Dual_EC_DRBG is explicitly disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 8 and was removed from SP 800-90A. It was found to potentially contain a backdoor allowing prediction of random outputs.
rules.remediation: Use CTR_DRBG with AES-256, Hash_DRBG with SHA-512, or HMAC_DRBG with SHA-512 as specified in SP 800-90A Rev.1. In Python: use secrets module or os.urandom().

rules.description: Hardcoded cryptographic keys violate SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 8.1 key management requirements. Keys embedded in source code are exposed to version control, logs, and all personnel with code access, violating the key confidentiality requirement.
rules.remediation: Store keys in environment variables, HSMs, or a secrets manager. Example: key = os.environ.get('ENCRYPTION_KEY')

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 8.1 and Section 4.3.4
rules.description: Hardcoded passwords and credentials violate SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 8.1 and 4.3.4 key and credential management requirements. Credentials in source code cannot be rotated without a code change and are exposed to all reviewers.
rules.remediation: Use environment variables or a secrets manager. Example: password = os.environ.get('APP_PASSWORD')

rules.nist_ref: SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 7; SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev.5 Section 5.3
rules.description: HMAC keys less than 112 bits (14 bytes) are disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 7. Short HMAC keys reduce the security strength of the MAC below the minimum approved level of 112 bits.
rules.remediation: Use HMAC keys of at least 112 bits (14 bytes). Recommended minimum is 256 bits (32 bytes). Example: key = secrets.token_bytes(32)

rules.description: SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are disallowed per NIST SP 800-52 Rev.2 Section 3.1. Known critical vulnerabilities include POODLE (SSLv3), BEAST (TLS 1.0), and DROWN (SSLv2).
rules.remediation: Configure minimum TLS 1.2. TLS 1.3 is preferred. Example: context.minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2

rules.description: Disabling TLS certificate verification violates SP 800-52 Rev.2 Section 3.4 which mandates server certificate validation to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.
rules.remediation: Always enable certificate verification. Example: requests.get(url, verify=True) or ssl_context.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_REQUIRED

rules.description: HMAC-MD5 uses MD5 which is not an approved hash function per SP 800-131A Rev.2 Section 9. SP 800-38B and SP 800-131A Section 7 require approved hash functions for all MAC generation.
rules.remediation: Use HMAC-SHA256 or HMAC-SHA512. Example: hmac.new(key, msg, hashlib.sha256)

rules.description: PBKDF2 with MD5 or SHA-1 is not recommended. SP 800-132 Section 5.3 requires NIST-approved PRFs for key derivation. SHA-1 is deprecated and MD5 is fully disallowed per SP 800-131A Rev.2.
rules.remediation: Use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 or PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512. Example: hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password, salt, 600000)

rules.description: PBKDF2 iteration counts below 100,000 are insufficient per SP 800-132 guidance. Low iteration counts make offline brute-force attacks feasible against derived keys.
rules.remediation: Use at least 600,000 iterations for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256. Example: hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', pwd, salt, 600000)
